preconditions.description: Input `n` is a positive integer between 1 and 10000 (inclusive).

postconditions.description: The returned string has exactly `n` characters.

postconditions.expression: all(c in {'0', '1'} for c in return_value)
postconditions.description: Every character in the returned string is either '0' or '1'.
The first character of the returned string is always '0'.

postconditions.expression: all(return_value[i] != return_value[i-1] for i in range(1, n) if (i & (i - 1)) == 0)
postconditions.description: For every position `i` (1-based) that is a power of 2, the character at `i` is the complement of the character at `i-1`. This enforces the Thue-Morse construction rule: the sequence is built by appending the complement of the existing sequence at each power-of-2 step.
